scope: Earlier-copy waveform localization with native Apple AudioToolbox AAC-LC M4A from the 234 exact source pairs of the frozen WAV/FLAC/FFmpeg AAC trial. All identities and noise mixtures are inherited. The three prior macOS clock probes are engineering examples, and this trial reuses known sources to measure codec transfer.
encodes: Render each prior submitted PCM to six seconds of 48000 Hz mono PCM16, then use macOS afconvert in AAC-LC mono M4A at nominal 64 and 96 kbps. Record both rates separately and keep the original earlier FLAC timing unchanged.
clock: Require one mono AAC-LC stream on the 1/48000 clock. Parse a complete iTunSMPB table and verify 2112 leading priming samples, 288000 valid samples, the exact remainder and coded extent, and contiguous 1024-sample packet timestamps from zero. Require the decoder's skipped samples and continuous output timeline to agree. Preserve relative playback time and native file ticks separately.
bit_rate: Keep the existing minimum measured stream bitrate of 60000 bps. Count all files excluded by that rule. The gate can qualify a rate with fewer than 5 percent bitrate exclusions only if those exclusions do not remove enough prior locations to fail the paired retention test.
criterion: Keep the existing waveform algorithm, localization overlap and acceptance criteria. Require full clock verification, useful WAV locations on at least 30 of 81 cut-and-paste deliveries, preservation of at least 85 percent of useful WAV locations after eligibility, a maximum of three net losses in any noise condition, and at most two new ordinary alerts from one reader. Count same-word resynthesis separately. Clock or bitrate eligibility is a file support condition, not AI confidence.
scope_limitation: These matched timing comparisons cannot establish AI authorship. Ordinary cuts, timing changes, and processing differences may also give a positive reading. They contribute zero weight to AI confidence.
